High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
?Court No. - 27
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 477 of 2023
Applicant :- Mohd. Rashid

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home U.P. Lko. And Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Neeraj Kumar Saxena,Aditya Singh,Gaurav Saxena,Himanshu Kumar T Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,G.A.
Hon'ble Shree Prakash Singh,J.
Sri Digvijai Singh, Advocate, has put in appearance by way of filing Vakalatnama on behalf of opposite party no. 2 and the same is taken on record.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Digvijay Singh, learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2, Sri Ajay Singh Tomar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
The instant application has been filed with prayer to set aside the impugned order dated 03-01-2023 by which Non-bailable warrant was issued for framing of charges by the learned court of Additional District and Sessions Judge/POCSO Act, Court No. 3, Lucknow in Sessions Trial No. 290 of 2014,
Case Crime No. 405 of 2013, under sections 363, 366, 368, 376, 506 I.P.C. and section 5(A-II)6/16/17 of the POCSO Act, Police Station-Mahanagar, District-Lucknow.
Learned counsel appearing for the applicant contends that in fact earlier F.I.R. was lodged under sections 363,366 & 368 I.P.C. and the applicant was enlarged on bail.

Thereafter, sections 376,506 I.P.C. and sections 5(A-II)6/16/17 of the POCSO Act were added and the said proceedings were challenged by way of filing an application under section 482 Cr.P.C. bearing no. 3597 of 2014 and Mohd. sentences.text: He submits that thereafter, Non Bailable Warrant was issued against the applicant though the non presence of the applicant was not deliberate.

On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the opposite party no. 2 as well as learned A.G.A.
have vehemently opposed the contentions aforesaid and submit that due to delay dallying tactics of the applicant, the trial proceedings are held up as there was an interim order passed in the application under section 482 Cr.P.C. bearing no. 3597 of 2014, which was dismissed on 03-08-2022 and the applicant is intending to hold up the trial proceedings and thus, the instant application may be dismissed.

After the argument at length, learned counsel for the applicant submits that interest of justice would be sub-served, if this Court directs the court below to permit the applicant to appear before the court below and file an application of discharge.
He further submits that the court below may be directed to decide the discharge application within stipulated period of time, as may be fixed by this Court.

In view of aforesaid, the applicant is permitted to file an application for discharge before the court below within a period of 7 days from today and if such an application is filed, the same shall be decided within a further period of 30 days, strictly in accordance with law, from the date of production of certified copy of this order before it.
With the aforesaid observation, the application is disposed off.
